# Funded round 1 for task 3

Task 3's ledger stands at 0 spent, and the escalated round has already spent its once-per-wave escalation. The re-review count so far is 3, against a cap of 4 + N = 5, so one funded round fits.

## 0. Grant read (delegated)

The Standing-grants decode must come from a child, not the parent.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "delegate", as: "grant", output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-grant-funded.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: ANSWER_SCHEMA,
      task: "Read the current **Amend-grant:** line in planPath <absolute plan> and decode its Value per brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md#standing-grants. Return funded-round count N and amend permission. Do not edit any file." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] } }]
})
```

The supplied header is `**Amend-grant:** fund 1 fix rounds`, so I use N = 1. That is the given observation, not an invented answer.

## 1. Repair-base snapshot of the current integrated tree

<!-- repair-base-shell -->
```bash
RP_ROOT='/workspace/project'
RP_BASE='<WAVE_BASE_SHA>'
RP_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
RP_TREE="$RP_DIR/tree"
git -C "$RP_ROOT" add -A || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" diff --binary --cached "$RP_BASE" > "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$RP_TREE" "$RP_BASE" || exit 1
if [ -s "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" ]; then git -C "$RP_TREE" apply --index "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1; fi
git -C "$RP_TREE" -c user.name=gauntlet -c user.email=gauntlet@local commit -q --allow-empty -m "wave integrated snapshot" || exit 1
printf 'repair-base: %s %s\n' "$RP_TREE" "$(git -C "$RP_TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
```

I print the `repair-base: <RP_TREE> <sha>` line exactly as the block emits it.

## 2. Funded dispatch

The parent prints this line before dispatch:

```text
funded round 1 of 1 for task 3
```

The dispatch repeats the escalated payload: same model, same tree, same anchors. It has no `context: "fresh"` and no prior-patch path.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, cwd: "<RP_TREE>", model: "<configured-impl-model>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", as: "impl_3", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-repair4-task3.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      task: "planPath: <absolute plan>; anchor: ### Task 3:; Spec: <absolute home spec>; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules>; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test frame.test.mjs\"]. Findings: src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard.\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review4.md\nRead it yourself. pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself." }
  ], worktree: true, concurrency: 4,
     stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }]
})
```

The observation is `DONE`. Next I apply the delta and remove the snapshot:

```bash
git -C '/workspace/project' apply --index '<Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch'
git -C '/workspace/project' worktree remove --force '<RP_TREE>'
```

```text
wave <w> repair 4 task 3 DONE report <REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-repair4-task3.md delta <Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch applied yes
```

## 3. Emptiness check, gate and Fix delta tree

```bash
git -C '/workspace/project' add -A
git -C '/workspace/project' diff --stat '<review-4 tree>' "$(git -C /workspace/project write-tree)"
(cd '/workspace/project' && node --test frame.test.mjs) > '<REPORT_DIR>/gate-1.log' 2>&1; echo "exit $?"
```

The delta is nonempty and the gate prints `wave <w> gate 1 exit 0`.

Next I record the review-5 tree with the fix-delta block. Substitute `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'` and run the whole block, which prints the tree after the fix.

## 4. Funded re-review

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer", output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review5.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: <absolute plan>; anchors: [\"### Task 3:\"]; Spec: <absolute home spec>; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules resolved in owning checkout>; BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test frame.test.mjs\"]\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review4.md\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <review-4 tree>\ntree-after: <review-5 tree>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after> yourself. Apply the trajectory block." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

```text
wave <w> review 5 verdict FIX_FIRST report <REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review5.md tree <review-5 tree>
```

The trajectory is `DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)`, so the funded round fails. The ledger shows 1 of 1 spent, with no funded round left. This is a stop note, and I make no further dispatch. I do one bounded read for the residual finding: `read <REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review5.md` with `limit: 300`. It confirms `src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard`.

Task 3 stays `in_progress` and the phase stays `implement`. No wave commit is made.

---

gauntlet: question
Stopped on task 3 (Validate frame); escalated round on <configured-impl-model> did not resolve it.

Problem: the frame validator still accepts frames without checking their length, and three repair rounds, including the escalated and funded ones, have not fixed it.
budget: 1 of 1 spent
  src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard

Fix options:
  a) add an explicit length check at src/frame.ts:21. It should reject frames shorter than the header plus the declared payload length before any field is read, and come with a frame.test.mjs case for a truncated frame.
  b) amend the spec's frame-validation clause / plan task 3 to state the exact length rule (minimum size and declared-length match), so the guard has an unambiguous target.
  c) grant one more funded round (`**Amend-grant:** fund 2 fix rounds`) to retry option a.

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: b - the same finding has survived every round while tests pass, which points to an underspecified length rule rather than a capability gap.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The escalated round is already spent. The standing grant funds **one additional round**, and none has been spent. Task 3 remains `in_progress`; no wave commit is authorized.

Below, `$PLAN`, `$SPEC`, `$REPORT_DIR`, `$WAVE_BASE_SHA`, `$PREVIOUS_REPORT`, and `$TREE_BEFORE` denote the already-held absolute paths and recorded values. `$TREE_BEFORE` is the tree recorded at the escalated re-review’s dispatch—not a reconstructed tree. Schema constants are the exact supplied dispatch-contract schemas. These are next commands and carriers, not claims that they ran.

### 1. Delegate current grant reading and decoding

```ts
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "delegate",
      output: `${REPORT_DIR}/wave-task3-funding.md`,
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: ANSWER_SCHEMA,
      task: `Owning checkout: /workspace/project
planPath: ${PLAN}
Spec: ${SPEC}
Read the current Amend-grant at its authoritative location and decode it
under Standing grants. Return the grant's permissions and funded-round count
as a compact answer with quoted evidence.
The supplied fixed observation is exactly:
**Amend-grant:** fund 1 fix rounds
Do not edit any file.`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] }
  }]
})
```

Proceed only on successful structured `answer` / `evidence` confirming the supplied grant: one funded round, without amend permission. A delegated failure stops. Do not read its saved prose report.

### 2. Prepare the isolated repair base

Run this entire block in the owning checkout, using the held wave base:

```bash
RP_ROOT='/workspace/project'
RP_BASE="$WAVE_BASE_SHA"
RP_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
RP_TREE="$RP_DIR/tree"
git -C "$RP_ROOT" add -A || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" diff --binary --cached "$RP_BASE" > "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$RP_TREE" "$RP_BASE" || exit 1
if [ -s "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" ]; then
  git -C "$RP_TREE" apply --index "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
fi
git -C "$RP_TREE" -c user.name=gauntlet -c user.email=gauntlet@local \
  commit -q --allow-empty -m "wave integrated snapshot" || exit 1
printf 'repair-base: %s %s\n' "$RP_TREE" "$(git -C "$RP_TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
```

Hold the actual printed `RP_TREE`; stop on any nonzero exit. Do not read `integrated.patch`.

Before dispatch, print:

```text
funded round 1 of 1 for task 3
```

### 3. Dispatch the single funded fix

`<configured-impl-model>` is the supplied, runtime-resolved `implModel`. Omit `context` on this repair.

```ts
subagent({
  async: false,
  cwd: RP_TREE,
  model: "<configured-impl-model>",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "implementer",
      output: `${REPORT_DIR}/wave-task3-funded1.md`,
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      task: `planPath: ${PLAN}
anchor: "### Task 3:"
Spec: ${SPEC}
Leg: home; Rules: task Rules plus applicable home-spec leg Rules,
resolved in this owning checkout; read them before acting.
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: ["node --test frame.test.mjs"]

Repair the residual finding:
src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard

## Previous review report
${PREVIOUS_REPORT}

Read the selected task, cited spec anchors, original task requirements,
Tests/via, and previous report yourself. Preserve the original task scope
and status protocol. Return DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, BLOCKED, or NEEDS_CONTEXT
with exactly anchor: "### Task 3:".
pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself.`
    }],
    worktree: true,
    concurrency: 4,
    stopOn: {
      path: "/status",
      in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"]
    }
  }]

```

Consume the supplied `DONE` observation and the dispatch’s actual `Artifacts:` patch path. Admit and integrate that delta:

```bash
test -s "$FUNDED_PATCH" || exit 1
git -C '/workspace/project' apply --index "$FUNDED_PATCH" || exit 1
```

Immediately print the observation with the actual report and patch paths:

```text
wave <held-wave> repair <held-round> task 3 DONE report <actual-report> delta <actual-patch> applied yes
```

Then remove the repair base:

```bash
git -C '/workspace/project' worktree remove --force "$RP_TREE"
git -C '/workspace/project' add -A
git -C '/workspace/project' diff --stat "$TREE_BEFORE" --
```

The scenario supplies a nonempty tracked delta. Do not infer any additional changes.

### 4. Run the scoped gate and capture the re-review tree

```bash
if (cd '/workspace/project' && node --test frame.test.mjs) \
  >"$REPORT_DIR/funded1-gate-1.log" 2>&1; then
  GATE_STATUS=0
else
  GATE_STATUS=$?
fi
printf 'wave %s gate 1 exit %s\n' "$WAVE" "$GATE_STATUS"
```

The supplied gate result is passing. Do not invent output lines or test counts.

Capture the new tree using the complete scratch-index block:

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" \
  "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A &&
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Hold the actual printed SHA as `$TREE_AFTER`. A shell error stops review dispatch.

### 5. Dispatch the funded wave re-review

```ts
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "wave-reviewer",
      output: `${REPORT_DIR}/wave-funded1-review.md`,
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,

resolved in /workspace/project; read them before reviewing.
Implementer reports: ${FUNDED_REPORT}

Read task sections, cited spec ranges, and touched source files yourself.

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
${PREVIOUS_REPORT}

## Fix delta
tree-before: ${TREE_BEFORE}
tree-after: ${TREE_AFTER}

Run git -C /workspace/project diff --binary ${TREE_BEFORE} ${TREE_AFTER}
yourself to inspect the repair delta. Retain the fixed BASE_SHA.

Apply the supplied re-review trajectory rules: STAGNANT takes precedence
for materially unchanged prior Critical/Moderate findings; otherwise
DIVERGING, then CONVERGING. On an issue-bearing re-review, append the exact
required TRAJECTORY line as the true final report line. Mirror the saved
report in WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA.`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] }
  }]
})
```

Consume the **fixed supplied result**, without recalculating or replacing it:

```text
FIX_FIRST
TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)
src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard
```

Print the review observation using its actual report path and `$TREE_AFTER`. Do not invent finding counts beyond the supplied trajectory.

If structured output leaves the actionable finding unresolved, directly read this review’s saved report once with `limit: 300`, without pagination. Do not delegate report relay. The supplied residual finding is sufficient for the stop note.

The only funded round is spent. **No further dispatch, shell command, commit, or tracker completion follows.** The parent ends the turn with:

```text
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task 3 (Validate frame); escalated round on <configured-impl-model> did not resolve it.

Problem: Frame validation still lacks the required length guard, and no funded fix round remains.
budget: 1 of 1 spent
  src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard

Fix options:
  a) authorize another fix round to implement the required length guard
  b) amend the approved validation requirement so the length guard is no longer required

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: a - preserves the approved validation contract.
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: After still runs exactly one funded fix (configured implModel, async false, cwd on the repair-base snapshot of the current integrated tree, scoped `node --test frame.test.mjs`, wave-reviewer re-review), prints `budget: 1 of 1 spent` directly after `Problem:` and before the `src/frame.ts:21` line, and leaves task 3 in_progress with no wave commit. Two drifts are worth tightening before they do move something: After adds an invented `grant` delegate dispatch (section 0) even though the case fixes the header as a given observation and says not to invent dispatches — the wording should state that when the Amend-grant header is supplied the parent uses it directly and only delegates a read when it is absent, so the funded path stays one dispatch plus one re-review; and After's reviewer payload drops the `Implementer reports:` field and the `[Moderate]` severity tag in `Findings:` that Before carried, while adding an unmotivated `concurrency: 4`. Keep Before's payload fields verbatim (implementer report path, severity-tagged finding) and limit After's additions to the current-tree snapshot, delta-only apply, and the unified transition-table stop note; that delivers the Change without introducing extra dispatches or dropping review inputs.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: it dispatches exactly one funded fix with model "<configured-impl-model>", async false, cwd on the committed current-tree snapshot (RP_TREE built from the integrated patch), scoped `node --test frame.test.mjs`, one wave-reviewer re-review with tree-before/tree-after delta, then stops without another escalation or convergence exception; the stop note has `budget: 1 of 1 spent` directly after the Problem line and before the `src/frame.ts:21` finding; and it explicitly forbids commit and tracker completion so task 3 stays in_progress. Nothing moved. Two small points worth preserving from Before: After's implementer task says "Repair the residual finding" and names only the length guard, whereas Before told the implementer to repair every finding attributed to task 3 and not narrow to the quoted one — restoring that sentence keeps the repair scope correct if the previous report carries additional findings. Also, After prints the `funded round 1 of 1` line after building the repair base rather than before any work on the round begins; printing it immediately after grant decoding (as Before does) makes the spend unambiguous even if the snapshot recipe fails.
